report:
The supplied paper does not establish complete original P16.5 in its claimed entire first-big domain. There is a concrete error in the actual moving-bundle identification (5.2), which also produces a false intersection-energy calculation in (5.4). The separate stronger physical weighted-convergence question is not the reason for this verdict.

I read the entire supplied standalone manuscript, all five canonical notes, the unchanged original criteria, the G0/G1 bodies and their scope restrictions, and the source register. G0 and G1 are treated only as caller grants in their stated scopes. Historical verdicts, artifact descriptions and source ledgers were not treated as mathematical evidence.

The decisive defect occurs in Section 5, immediately before (5.2). On a total determination, write the pulled fixed divisor as T_m=T_m^hor+T_m^ver. Removing its horizontal part from the original complete system leaves the actual bundle
p^*A_m+D+T_m^ver+cF,
not p^*A_m+D+cF. After resolving the residual ideal, its moving bundle must therefore retain +T_m^ver before subtracting the effective residual vertical base divisor. Equation (5.2) omits this term. Section 9 correctly retains it in (9.2), but does not correct the earlier identification or its intersection calculations.

Here is an explicit counterexample within the retained domain. Work over the trivially valued algebraic closure of Q. Let X=Bl_p(P^2), let H be the pulled hyperplane class, and let E be the exceptional curve. Take the actual integral bundle L=H+E. Since H restricts trivially to E and E^2=-1, the restriction exact sequences give
H^0(X,mL)=s_E^m H^0(X,mH)
for every m≥1. Thus L is big, V=1, its complete fixed part is mE, and A_m=H and T_m=E in every degree. It is nonample since L·E=-1.

Let p:Y→X×P^1 be the blowup of E×{0}, and denote its exceptional divisor by G. This is a smooth equivariant projective model, product away from zero. On it,
p^*E=E^hor+G.
Choose D=-G. The original model obstacle is f_D=-min(v(E),1). Every original section s_E^m a extends with weight zero: its pulled fixed factor already vanishes to order m along G. Positive weights are impossible by evaluation at v_0. Consequently the entire relative lattice has weights w_mj=0. Its full-section energy intercept is therefore 0.

For an integral time twist c>1, the complete absolute system is the system of
p^*L-G+cF=p^*H+E^hor+cF.
Its fixed divisor is exactly mE^hor. After removing that horizontal divisor, the residual base ideal is the unit ideal, so its residual vertical base divisor is zero. The actual generated moving bundle is p^*H+cF, and the actual physical quotient scalar is zero.

Equation (5.2), with that same residual base divisor, instead gives p^*H-G+cF. These are different actual bundles. Moreover G^3=1, p^*H·G^2=F·G^2=0, and H^2=1. Hence
(p^*H+cF)^3=3c,
whereas
(p^*H-G+cF)^3=3c-1.
The intersection expression displayed in (5.4), using the bundle specified in (5.2), consequently gives -1/3 in every degree. Its asserted limit E(P_theta(f_D)) is 0, as follows directly from the zero full-lattice weights and Section 4's intercept definition. The discrepancy persists through the degree limit.

This is an actual geometric error, not merely a numerical-equivalence issue, rounding error, missing multiplicity, or harmless wording correction. Redefining G_m,D^ver as the residual base divisor minus mT_m^ver would make it generally signed and would change its stated origin as a residual ideal's base divisor. No such convention is supplied. A repair must reconstruct the actual moving systems and recheck their intersections, domination bounds and limits; I have not silently substituted that repaired argument.

The remaining proof audit gives the following dependency conclusions. Sections 2–3's literal ample embedding, section minorants, old-pole comparison, guarded directed flattening and normalized compactness have the appropriate logical structure under G0/G1 and the ample separator result. The comparison extension at poles is explicitly distinguished from subtraction of infinities. Section 4's full flag, time-twist intercept, raw coefficient derivatives and finite-coordinate supporting planes do not themselves remove the Section 5 error. The complete-system cofinality argument uses actual sections after rational interior approximation; it does not require positive-product multilinearity. The missing-volume term in (5.5) has the correct sign and must indeed remain until the moving limit at a fixed finite majorant.

In Section 6, I checked the tangent orientation and coefficient n-j, the SNC zero-row quadratic identity, the midpoint kernel and the raw generic term in the absolute estimate. However, the genuine contraction (6.7) explicitly transfers auxiliary energies through (5.4). That transfer is not established with the stated moving bundle. Accordingly, its finite-energy pole construction and the later intrinsic integrability/coercivity deductions cannot be credited unconditionally.

Section 7's signed margin is arithmetically sufficient: c_s-B_s/V≥c-B/V-|s|H_0, so (7.2) protects both perturbation signs. The deficient derivative argument retains coefficientwise positivity and the B/c missing mass. Those checks do not establish the subsequent weighted and integrability conclusions that depend on the failed finite-moving transfer. Section 8's proposed continuous-Radon passages can avoid measurable-net monotone convergence because the fixed canonical relative costs are continuous on U; nevertheless its absolute estimates and whole planes depend on the preceding auxiliary identification.

Section 9's restricted lattice (9.2) correctly includes T^ver. Exact subspace/quotient trace additivity and the argument forcing positivity from norm and constant value are sound finite-dimensional steps. Both signs of the fixed-upper Morse squeeze require the actual nef approximants to the specified restricted bundle. The bounded physical identification also uses the earlier whole planes and finite-moving limits. Its correct restricted-lattice formula is not an independent proof repairing all of Section 5.

Sections 10–11 fix their interpolation matrices before limits and distinguish genuine weighted continuity from paired physical quotient moments. The cap total-variation estimate, fixed-cap ordering and barycenter comparison are conditional finite arguments of the stated form. But the construction of the joint filter and its subsequent identifications invoke the finite-list energy and weak limits (5.4). They therefore do not supply an unconditional replacement foundation after the defect above. The two terms of (11.4) remain separate, as the paper says; no supported infinities may be subtracted.

Section 12's pre-attainment strategy does not inherently require an inverse equation to construct the atomic approximants. Its finite-coordinate continuity, separate fixed-test limit before the supremum, both stationarity signs and independent divisorial probes are logically appropriate provided the preceding absolute estimates and genuine operator have been established. Here those antecedents remain unsupported. The same applies to Section 13: the fixed ramp's wrong-winner implication and its order of limits are appropriate for independent nets, but locality and comparison still depend on the unestablished operator identifications. Thus actual attainment and every-solution uniqueness have not been proved by this manuscript.

The numerical-zero classification in Section 14 is independently supported by the ample embedding and integer-tensor coordinate bounds: the cone consists of constants, including for nontorsion numerically trivial bundles, and the positive raw mass tends to zero. The P^1×P^1 example correctly obstructs uniqueness for the larger nonzero zero-volume raw-top equation. The negligible-set deduction, however, needs the genuine E1 pole transfer whose contraction foundation is affected above.

Note n1 inherits the false actual moving identification. Notes n2–n4 depend on those foundations and do not provide an independent repair. Note n3 correctly acknowledges that paired quotient moments do not establish fixed-original-unbounded physical weighted convergence. Note n5's complete-scope candidate claim is therefore not justified.

The unchanged original criteria require the genuine original-carrier operator, intrinsic finite-energy targets, comparison, actual existence and uniqueness. They do not explicitly require weighted convergence of every fixed unbounded original test against every physical auxiliary output, whose stages need not belong to original E1. A proved genuine weighted route could therefore suffice. This separate stronger gap alone would not warrant FAIL. Here the purported weaker route relies on the false finite-moving identification, so it has not established original completion either.

Independent primary reading used the URLs in passages. Literal retrieved coordinates are: premise 0, BJ v4 L3996–4022, PDF page index 56; premise 1, BJ L10614–10647, page index 131, together with L3767–3774 for the pole convention; premise 2, BFJ v2 L250–280 and L310–441; premise 3, BFJ L445–535; premise 4, Lazarsfeld–Mustata v1 L1010–1175; premise 5, that source L1414–1631, including the arbitrary-field clarification; premise 6, Bierstone–Milman v1 Theorems 1.1 and 1.3, especially L160–209; premise 7, DEL v2 L429–431; premise 8, BJ L512–528, Lazarsfeld Chapter 6 L385–437, and Stacks 28.27.12, especially L117–124. The general-field Kodaira application can also be checked directly using section growth versus O(m^(d-1)) restriction growth. I do not claim an exhaustive independent reconstruction of the entire principalization algorithm; that external proof check remains unsettled. The concrete counterexample above is self-contained and does not depend on that unsettled check, so the verdict is FAIL rather than INCONCLUSIVE.

G0/G1 are excluded from the external-premise list. The additional task passage attached to premise 1 records the caller-granted ample foundation used in that application. No silent harmless wording correction was used to obtain this verdict.

passages.statement: For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an actual ample rational bundle Omega, the usc regularization of the raw supremum of any uniformly bounded-above family of genuine Omega-psh functions agrees with that raw supremum at every divisorial point. [BJ v4, Theorem 5.6 and Lemma 5.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class having the envelope property, every negligible subset is contained in the pole set of a genuine psh function; the pole function may be taken in any specified ample class. [BJ v4, Theorem 13.17 and Lemma 4.35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

passages.statement: On smooth projective varieties over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, positive products of big real Cartier b-classes are least upper bounds of products of dominated nef Cartier b-classes; they are monotone, homogeneous and continuous on the big cone, and agree with ordinary products on nef classes. Their defining directed bounded approximants converge weakly. [BFJ v2, Section 2](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0608260v2).

On a smooth projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, volume is C1 on the big cone, with Dvol_alpha(H)=d<alpha^(d-1)>·H. For nef beta and nef big omega satisfying beta<=omega and omega±H nef, vol(beta+tH)>=beta^d+d t beta^(d-1)·H-Ct^2 for |t|<=1, where C depends only on omega^d. Volume is continuous on all classes, and its d-th root is concave on the pseudoeffective cone. [BFJ v2, Theorem A, Corollary 3.4 and Theorem 2.16](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0608260v2).
passages.quote: The volume function is $\mathcal{C}^{1}$-differentiable on the big cone of $N^{1}(X)$.

Characteristic-zero varieties admit functorial resolution by finite sequences of blowups with smooth centers. On a smooth characteristic-zero variety with an SNC boundary, a nonzero coherent ideal admits functorial principalization by such blowups compatible with the boundary. These constructions can be made equivariant for algebraic group actions preserving the data. [Bierstone–Milman v1, Theorems 1.1 and 1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702375v1).

passages.statement: For an actual big rational bundle N and an actual ample bundle A on a smooth integral projective variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, there exist a positive rational a and an effective rational Cartier divisor E with an actual rational-bundle identity N=aA+E.
